paragraphs.title: The Lord Commands a Way of Life

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Moses
Pharaoh
The king of Canaan
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “The Lord spake unto Moses.”

easy.question: Whose practices were the Israelites commanded not to follow?
answers: Jerusalem and Hebron
Egypt and Canaan
Babylon and Assyria
easy.explanation: The passage says not to follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan.

easy.question: What does the passage promise to those who keep the Lord’s laws and judgments?
answers: Great wealth
Victory in war
Life
easy.explanation: The verse says, “which if a man do, he shall live in them.”

medium.question: What is the main order given in these verses?
answers: Do not imitate the nations; instead, follow the Lord’s laws
Leave Egypt and return there
Learn Canaan’s laws before the Lord’s laws
medium.explanation: The Israelites are first told not to follow Egypt and Canaan, and then to keep the Lord’s laws.

medium.question: In the phrase “neither shall ye walk in their ordinances,” what does “their ordinances” mean?
answers: Their clothing
Their customs and rules
Their houses
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the customs and rules of Egypt and Canaan.

medium.question: Why does the passage mention both Egypt and Canaan?
answers: The Israelites lived in both lands
Both lands were in the wilderness
To warn them about both their past and the land ahead
medium.explanation: Egypt was where the Israelites had lived, while Canaan was the land to which the Lord was bringing them.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repeated phrase “I am the Lord your God”?
answers: The commands are based on the Lord’s authority
The people may choose whether to obey
The verses concern only Egypt
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the Lord is the source of the commands and that Israel’s identity is connected to him.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between “doings” and “ordinances” in verse 3?
answers: Doings refer to the future, while ordinances refer to the past
Doings refer to behavior, while ordinances refer to customs or rules
They have exactly the same meaning
challenge.explanation: The verse forbids both adopting the nations’ behavior and following their customs.

challenge.question: What connection between keeping the commandments and life is emphasized at the end of the passage?
answers: Keeping them makes a person move to another land
Keeping them makes a person stronger than others
Keeping them is presented as a way of life before the Lord
challenge.explanation: The words “he shall live in them” present obedience to the Lord’s laws as a way of life, not merely a list of rules.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repeated phrase “I am the Lord your God”?
answers: The commands are based on the Lord’s authority
The people may choose whether to obey
The verses concern only Egypt
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the Lord is the source of the commands and that Israel’s identity is connected to him.

questions.question: What is the main difference between “doings” and “ordinances” in verse 3?
answers: Doings refer to the future, while ordinances refer to the past
Doings refer to behavior, while ordinances refer to customs or rules
They have exactly the same meaning
questions.explanation: The verse forbids both adopting the nations’ behavior and following their customs.

questions.question: What connection between keeping the commandments and life is emphasized at the end of the passage?
answers: Keeping them makes a person move to another land
Keeping them makes a person stronger than others
Keeping them is presented as a way of life before the Lord
questions.explanation: The words “he shall live in them” present obedience to the Lord’s laws as a way of life, not merely a list of rules.

easy.question: What general prohibition appears in verse 6?
answers: Do not approach a close relative to uncover their nakedness
Do not speak with relatives
Do not live with relatives
easy.explanation: Verse 6 commands that no one approach a close relative to uncover their nakedness.

easy.question: Whose nakedness must not be uncovered according to verse 7?
answers: The neighbor’s
The sister’s only
The father’s and mother’s
easy.explanation: Verse 7 explicitly mentions the father and the mother.

easy.question: Who is included in the prohibition in verse 9?
answers: Only a cousin
A sister who is the daughter of one’s father or mother
Any woman who is not a relative
easy.explanation: Verse 9 refers to a sister who is the daughter of one’s father or mother.

medium.question: Why must the nakedness of the father’s wife not be uncovered according to verse 8?
answers: Because it is identified with the father’s nakedness
Because she is the family’s neighbor
Because she is the man’s daughter
medium.explanation: The verse says, “it is thy father’s nakedness,” linking the prohibition to her position as the father’s wife.

medium.question: What does the phrase “born at home” mean in the context of the sister described in verse 9?
answers: A sister unrelated to the family
A sister born within the household or family
A sister who lives in another house
medium.explanation: The verse describes a sister who is the daughter of one’s father or mother, whether born at home or elsewhere.

medium.question: Why is the nakedness of a son’s daughter or daughter’s daughter forbidden in verse 10?
answers: Because they are the person’s sisters
Because they are the father’s wives
Because the verse identifies them as the person’s own nakedness
medium.explanation: The verse explains the prohibition by saying, “for theirs is thine own nakedness.”

challenge.question: What special detail is given in verse 11 about the father’s wife’s daughter?
answers: She is the father’s daughter and is therefore the person’s sister
She is only the mother’s daughter
She is not a relative
challenge.explanation: The verse calls her the father’s daughter and adds, “she is thy sister,” even though she is the father’s wife’s daughter.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the repeated reference to “thy father’s nakedness” in verses 7–8?
answers: The prohibition applies only to the father himself
A relationship with the mother or father’s wife also affects the family relationship with the father
The mother and the father’s wife are always the same person
challenge.explanation: In both verses, the relationship to the father is central: one concerns his mother and the other his wife.

challenge.question: What does the structure of verse 6, followed by the list in verses 7–11, show?
answers: The prohibition applies only to a sister
The verses concern only unrelated women
A broad rule is given first, followed by examples of relatives
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 gives the general prohibition, and the following verses list particular family members.

questions.question: What special detail is given in verse 11 about the father’s wife’s daughter?
answers: She is the father’s daughter and is therefore the person’s sister
She is only the mother’s daughter
She is not a relative
questions.explanation: The verse calls her the father’s daughter and adds, “she is thy sister,” even though she is the father’s wife’s daughter.

questions.question: What can be understood from the repeated reference to “thy father’s nakedness” in verses 7–8?
answers: The prohibition applies only to the father himself
A relationship with the mother or father’s wife also affects the family relationship with the father
The mother and the father’s wife are always the same person
questions.explanation: In both verses, the relationship to the father is central: one concerns his mother and the other his wife.

questions.question: What does the structure of verse 6, followed by the list in verses 7–11, show?
answers: The prohibition applies only to a sister
The verses concern only unrelated women
A broad rule is given first, followed by examples of relatives
questions.explanation: Verse 6 gives the general prohibition, and the following verses list particular family members.

easy.question: Whose nakedness must not be uncovered in verse 12?
answers: The father’s sister
The daughter
The brother’s wife
easy.explanation: Verse 12 forbids uncovering the nakedness of the father’s sister.

easy.question: Who is the daughter-in-law mentioned in verse 15?
answers: Your brother’s wife
Your son’s wife
Your mother’s sister
easy.explanation: The verse explains, “she is thy son’s wife.”

easy.question: What is forbidden in verse 18?
answers: Taking a woman and her mother
Uncovering the father’s sister’s nakedness
Taking a wife in addition to her sister
easy.explanation: Verse 18 says, “Neither shalt thou take a wife to her sister.”

medium.question: What idea is shared by most of the prohibitions in verses 12–16?
answers: Prohibitions against sexual relations with close relatives
A ban on eating certain foods
A ban on living in a certain land
medium.explanation: The verses list female relatives whose nakedness must not be uncovered, including an aunt, a daughter-in-law, and a brother’s wife.

medium.question: In the phrase “she is thy father’s near kinswoman,” what does “near kinswoman” mean?
answers: Property
A close female relative
An enemy
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies the father’s sister as a close family member.

medium.question: Which prohibition appears immediately after the prohibition concerning a brother’s wife?
answers: Taking a wife and her sister
The father’s wife
A woman and her daughter or granddaughter
medium.explanation: Verse 17 follows verse 16 and forbids taking a woman together with her daughter or granddaughter.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “they are her near kinswomen; it is wickedness” in verse 17 emphasize?
answers: They are close relatives, making the act especially serious
The women are unrelated to one another
The prohibition concerns only where they live
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the women are close relatives and calls the relationship wickedness.

challenge.question: What special detail is added at the end of verse 18?
answers: The woman is the son’s wife
The prohibition applies while the sister is alive
The woman is the father’s sister
challenge.explanation: The verse adds “beside the other in her life time,” referring to the sister while she is still alive.

challenge.question: Who is the “aunt” mentioned in verse 14?
answers: The mother’s sister
The brother’s daughter
The father’s brother’s wife
challenge.explanation: The verse says she is the wife of the father’s brother and calls her the person’s aunt.

questions.question: What does the phrase “they are her near kinswomen; it is wickedness” in verse 17 emphasize?
answers: They are close relatives, making the act especially serious
The women are unrelated to one another
The prohibition concerns only where they live
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the women are close relatives and calls the relationship wickedness.

questions.question: What special detail is added at the end of verse 18?
answers: The woman is the son’s wife
The prohibition applies while the sister is alive
The woman is the father’s sister
questions.explanation: The verse adds “beside the other in her life time,” referring to the sister while she is still alive.

questions.question: Who is the “aunt” mentioned in verse 14?
answers: The mother’s sister
The brother’s daughter
The father’s brother’s wife
questions.explanation: The verse says she is the wife of the father’s brother and calls her the person’s aunt.

paragraphs.title: The Holiness of Marriage and the Body

easy.question: What is forbidden regarding a woman “put apart for her uncleanness” in verse 19?
answers: Approaching her to uncover her nakedness
Speaking with her
Eating in her house
easy.explanation: The verse says, “thou shalt not approach unto a woman to uncover her nakedness” during her uncleanness.

easy.question: With whom must a man not have sexual relations according to verse 20?
answers: His sister
His neighbor’s wife
His daughter
easy.explanation: The verse forbids lying carnally with one’s neighbor’s wife.

easy.question: What must not be done with one’s offspring according to verse 21?
answers: Sent to another land
Taught a trade
Passed through the fire to Molech
easy.explanation: The verse says, “thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech.”

medium.question: What connection does the passage make between giving offspring to Molech and profaning God’s name?
answers: Giving offspring to Molech honors God’s name
The passage warns that the act profanes God’s name
The passage makes no connection between them
medium.explanation: Immediately after the prohibition, the verse says, “neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God.”

medium.question: In the phrase “thy neighbour’s wife,” what does “neighbour” refer to?
answers: An enemy
A king
Another person or fellow member of the community
medium.explanation: The context makes clear that the prohibition concerns another person’s wife.

medium.question: What order of topics appears in verses 19–21?
answers: A woman in her uncleanness, a neighbor’s wife, and giving offspring to Molech
Giving offspring to Molech, a neighbor’s wife, and a woman in her uncleanness
A neighbor’s wife, worship, and then Sabbath laws
medium.explanation: Verse 19 concerns a woman in her uncleanness, verse 20 a neighbor’s wife, and verse 21 Molech.

challenge.question: What prominent feature do these three verses share?
answers: They present prohibitions involving boundaries of holiness and sexual or religious conduct
They all concern property laws
They all describe events from the past
challenge.explanation: The verses prohibit forbidden sexual relations and giving offspring to Molech, connecting both with uncleanness and profaning God’s name.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “to defile thyself with her” refer to?
answers: Molech
The neighbor’s wife
The offspring
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the neighbor’s wife mentioned immediately before it.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the movement in verse 21 from the prohibition to “neither shalt thou profane”?
answers: The prohibition concerns only physical harm
The act is treated as merely private
The act is also viewed as an offense against the holiness of God’s name
challenge.explanation: The verse adds a religious dimension: the act does not merely harm a person but profanes God’s name.

questions.question: What prominent feature do these three verses share?
answers: They present prohibitions involving boundaries of holiness and sexual or religious conduct
They all concern property laws
They all describe events from the past
questions.explanation: The verses prohibit forbidden sexual relations and giving offspring to Molech, connecting both with uncleanness and profaning God’s name.

questions.question: What does the phrase “to defile thyself with her” refer to?
answers: Molech
The neighbor’s wife
The offspring
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the neighbor’s wife mentioned immediately before it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the movement in verse 21 from the prohibition to “neither shalt thou profane”?
answers: The prohibition concerns only physical harm
The act is treated as merely private
The act is also viewed as an offense against the holiness of God’s name
questions.explanation: The verse adds a religious dimension: the act does not merely harm a person but profanes God’s name.

easy.question: What is forbidden in verse 22?
answers: Lying with a male
Eating with a male
Speaking with a male
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind.”

easy.question: With whom is lying forbidden in verse 23?
answers: A woman
An animal
A friend
easy.explanation: The verse forbids lying with any beast.

easy.question: How does verse 23 describe the act involving an animal?
answers: As a blessing
As wisdom
As confusion
easy.explanation: The verse ends by calling the act “confusion.”

medium.question: What do the two verses have in common?
answers: Both concern prohibitions involving sexual relations
Both concern dietary laws
Both concern property laws
medium.explanation: Both verses describe sexual acts forbidden by the Torah.

medium.question: How does verse 22 describe the prohibited act?
answers: As a joyful deed
As an abomination
As an ordinary act
medium.explanation: The verse ends by saying, “it is abomination.”

medium.question: What is the order of topics in these verses?
answers: First a prohibition involving a male, then prohibitions involving an animal
First a prohibition involving food, then one involving drink
First a prohibition involving a male, then a marriage law
medium.explanation: Verse 22 concerns a male, while verse 23 concerns sexual acts involving an animal.

challenge.question: What special detail appears in verse 23 compared with verse 22?
answers: The verse also addresses a woman and describes her action with an animal
The verse cancels the previous prohibition
The verse concerns thoughts rather than actions
challenge.explanation: Verse 23 also says that a woman must not stand before an animal to lie down with it.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “as with womankind” in verse 22 mean?
answers: It permits lying with a woman
It compares the act to the way one lies with a woman
It commands a person to marry a woman
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the manner of the act, while the prohibition itself concerns lying with a male.

challenge.question: What is an accurate comparison of the endings of the two verses?
answers: Both say the act is a commandment
Neither describes the seriousness of the act
Each ends with a term describing the act negatively
challenge.explanation: Verse 22 ends with “it is abomination,” and verse 23 ends with “it is confusion.”

questions.question: What special detail appears in verse 23 compared with verse 22?
answers: The verse also addresses a woman and describes her action with an animal
The verse cancels the previous prohibition
The verse concerns thoughts rather than actions
questions.explanation: Verse 23 also says that a woman must not stand before an animal to lie down with it.

questions.question: What does the phrase “as with womankind” in verse 22 mean?
answers: It permits lying with a woman
It compares the act to the way one lies with a woman
It commands a person to marry a woman
questions.explanation: The phrase describes the manner of the act, while the prohibition itself concerns lying with a male.

questions.question: What is an accurate comparison of the endings of the two verses?
answers: Both say the act is a commandment
Neither describes the seriousness of the act
Each ends with a term describing the act negatively
questions.explanation: Verse 22 ends with “it is abomination,” and verse 23 ends with “it is confusion.”

easy.question: What does the passage command the Israelites?
answers: Do not defile yourselves with these things
Leave the land
Fight the nations
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things.”

easy.question: Who had been defiled by these acts according to the passage?
answers: The Israelites
The nations
The wilderness inhabitants
easy.explanation: The passage says, “in all these the nations are defiled.”

easy.question: What did the land do to its inhabitants?
answers: It welcomed them
It hid them
It vomited them out
easy.explanation: The passage says, “the land itself vomiteth out her inhabitants.”

medium.question: What connection does the passage make between the nations’ defilement and the land?
answers: The land was defiled by the acts of its inhabitants
The land purified its inhabitants
The nations were purified by the land
medium.explanation: The verses connect the nations’ acts with the defilement of the land and its expulsion of the inhabitants.

medium.question: In the phrase “I do visit the iniquity thereof upon it,” what does “visit” mean?
answers: Simply remember
Punish and call the sin to account
Bless
medium.explanation: In this context, “visit” means to judge or punish the land for its iniquity.

medium.question: Why are the nations who were defiled mentioned before the command to the Israelites?
answers: To tell the story of their journey
To announce that they would remain forever
To warn the Israelites not to follow their ways
medium.explanation: The nations serve as an example of forbidden conduct and of the serious result of defiling the land.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “the land is defiled”?
answers: Wrongdoing affects not only people but also the land
The land became cleaner
The land immediately became uninhabited
challenge.explanation: The passage portrays the land as being defiled by the acts committed in it.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: The land vomits out its inhabitants, and then they are defiled
The land is defiled, its iniquity is judged, and it vomits out its inhabitants
The nations are purified, and then the land welcomes them
challenge.explanation: The sequence is that the land is defiled, its iniquity is judged, and it finally vomits out its inhabitants.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the statement that the Lord casts the nations out before Israel?
answers: The nations left solely by their own choice
The nations had never lived in the land
Their removal is connected with their defilement and conduct
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the nations’ defilement with their being cast out before Israel.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “the land is defiled”?
answers: Wrongdoing affects not only people but also the land
The land became cleaner
The land immediately became uninhabited
questions.explanation: The passage portrays the land as being defiled by the acts committed in it.

questions.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: The land vomits out its inhabitants, and then they are defiled
The land is defiled, its iniquity is judged, and it vomits out its inhabitants
The nations are purified, and then the land welcomes them
questions.explanation: The sequence is that the land is defiled, its iniquity is judged, and it finally vomits out its inhabitants.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that the Lord casts the nations out before Israel?
answers: The nations left solely by their own choice
The nations had never lived in the land
Their removal is connected with their defilement and conduct
questions.explanation: The passage connects the nations’ defilement with their being cast out before Israel.

paragraphs.title: Keeping the Land for All Its Inhabitants

easy.question: Who is commanded to keep the Lord’s laws and not commit these abominations?
answers: The native-born and the stranger
Only the kings of the land
Only the former inhabitants of the land
easy.explanation: The passage addresses both the people of the nation and the stranger living among them.

easy.question: What do the verses warn against?
answers: Leaving the land
Committing the abominations
Eating the fruit of the land
easy.explanation: The passage commands the people not to commit any of these abominations.

easy.question: What may happen to the land when it is defiled?
answers: It will flourish more
It will remain unchanged
It will vomit out its inhabitants
easy.explanation: The passage warns that the land may vomit out those who defile it.

medium.question: Why might the land vomit out its inhabitants?
answers: Because they defile it with abominations
Because it does not have enough water
Because a stranger may not live there
medium.explanation: The expulsion is presented as the result of committing abominations and defiling the land.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: The land vomits out the people, and then they defile it
The former inhabitants commit abominations, the land is defiled, and it vomits them out
The people keep the laws, and then the land is defiled
medium.explanation: The former inhabitants committed abominations; the land was defiled and eventually vomited them out.

medium.question: In the phrase “that the land spue not you out also,” what does “spue out” mean?
answers: Bless you
Cover you
Remove or drive you out
medium.explanation: In this context, the phrase means to expel or drive people from the land.

challenge.question: What connection does the passage emphasize between a person’s conduct and his fate in the land?
answers: Defiling conduct may lead to expulsion from the land
There is no connection between conduct and living in the land
Only a person’s ancestry determines whether he remains
challenge.explanation: The passage directly connects defiling the land with the possibility that it will expel its inhabitants.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the warning being addressed to both the native-born and the stranger?
answers: Only the stranger must obey the laws
The duty to avoid the abominations applies to all who live in the land
The native-born are exempt from judgment
challenge.explanation: Mentioning both groups shows that the prohibition applies to everyone living in the land.

challenge.question: Why does the passage mention that the land had already vomited out the nation that lived there before Israel?
answers: To describe the size of the land
To say that the former nation was righteous
To warn that Israel could be punished in the same way
challenge.explanation: The earlier nation’s fate warns Israel that they too could be expelled if they defile the land.

questions.question: What connection does the passage emphasize between a person’s conduct and his fate in the land?
answers: Defiling conduct may lead to expulsion from the land
There is no connection between conduct and living in the land
Only a person’s ancestry determines whether he remains
questions.explanation: The passage directly connects defiling the land with the possibility that it will expel its inhabitants.

questions.question: What can be learned from the warning being addressed to both the native-born and the stranger?
answers: Only the stranger must obey the laws
The duty to avoid the abominations applies to all who live in the land
The native-born are exempt from judgment
questions.explanation: Mentioning both groups shows that the prohibition applies to everyone living in the land.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that the land had already vomited out the nation that lived there before Israel?
answers: To describe the size of the land
To say that the former nation was righteous
To warn that Israel could be punished in the same way
questions.explanation: The earlier nation’s fate warns Israel that they too could be expelled if they defile the land.

easy.question: What will happen to anyone who commits the abominations described in the passage?
answers: They will be cut off from among their people
They will receive a special position
They will move to another land
easy.explanation: The passage says that those who commit the abominations will be cut off from among their people.

easy.question: What does the Lord command the people to guard against?
answers: Wars
The abominable customs
Foods
easy.explanation: The passage commands them to keep the Lord’s ordinance and not follow the abominable customs.

easy.question: Who speaks at the end of the passage?
answers: Moses
The people
The Lord their God
easy.explanation: The passage ends with, “I am the Lord your God.”

medium.question: What connection does verse 29 make between committing abominations and punishment?
answers: Committing them leads to being cut off from the people
Committing them brings blessing to the family
Committing them makes a person a leader
medium.explanation: The verse directly connects the abominations with being cut off from the people.

medium.question: In “keep mine ordinance,” what does “mine ordinance” refer to?
answers: A night watch
The laws and commandments to be obeyed
Memories of the past
medium.explanation: The context shows that it refers to the duties and commandments given by the Lord.

medium.question: What is the sequence of ideas in the two verses?
answers: First the people are defiled, and then the commandments are given
First the punishment is described, and then the people are warned to avoid the acts
First the Exodus is described, and then the entry into the land
medium.explanation: Verse 29 describes the punishment, while verse 30 warns the people to avoid the abominations.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “cut off from among their people”?
answers: The punishment involves removal from the community or nation
The person is sent into the middle of the people
The act is permitted only within the family
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that those who commit the abominations will be separated or removed from their community.

challenge.question: Why does the passage refer to customs practiced by those who came before Israel?
answers: To teach that the customs are entirely new
To warn Israel not to imitate the earlier nations
To command the people to remember the nations’ names
challenge.explanation: The reference points to practices that came before and warns Israel not to follow them.

challenge.question: What does the image of being defiled by these acts mean in context?
answers: The people should avoid the abominations because they damage spiritual and moral purity
People must wash after every ordinary act
People must avoid contact with everyone else
challenge.explanation: Here, defilement describes spiritual and moral corruption, not merely physical dirt.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “cut off from among their people”?
answers: The punishment involves removal from the community or nation
The person is sent into the middle of the people
The act is permitted only within the family
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that those who commit the abominations will be separated or removed from their community.

questions.question: Why does the passage refer to customs practiced by those who came before Israel?
answers: To teach that the customs are entirely new
To warn Israel not to imitate the earlier nations
To command the people to remember the nations’ names
questions.explanation: The reference points to practices that came before and warns Israel not to follow them.

questions.question: What does the image of being defiled by these acts mean in context?
answers: The people should avoid the abominations because they damage spiritual and moral purity
People must wash after every ordinary act
People must avoid contact with everyone else
questions.explanation: Here, defilement describes spiritual and moral corruption, not merely physical dirt.
